data: Before we head out, how about we agree to 10 tons each this month? That gives each of us $10,000 and leaves 50 tons to reproduce, bringing the lake back to 100 next month. It’s the largest total catch we can sustain month after month, shared equally. My family has fished here for years, and I want this lake to keep supporting all our families. We can review everyone’s catches afterward and stick with the same limits if the lake stays full. John, would you agree?

I’m in, Luke—10 tons for me. My family taught me to leave enough fish for the next trip, and this agreement gives all five families a steady income without draining the lake. Let’s check the catches together each month and agree on lower limits if the stock falls below 100 tons. Kate, are you willing to join us?

Count me in for 10 tons too. A steady catch protects both our incomes and the village’s future. If anyone needs more in a particular month, let’s discuss a whole-ton swap within the 50-ton total rather than increase the total catch. Kate, does that work for you?

I’m in for 10 tons. This lake supports more than our own households, and I want it healthy for the next generation too. Emma’s swap idea works for me, provided we agree beforehand and keep the total at 50 tons. Jack, will you join us at 10 tons?

I’m in—10 tons for me. My family taught me to look after the lake that feeds us, and this gives us a fair catch while keeping it healthy. Let’s check the results together afterward; any whole-ton swaps need everyone’s agreement before fishing and must stay within our 50-ton total. See you at the docks.
Agreed—10 tons each this month, with no swaps requested. Thanks, everyone. Let’s meet after the catches are reported to check the lake and plan next month. See you at the docks!
